name: AC ChievoVerona
content:
AC ChievoVerona was an Italian football club from Chievo, a small district of Verona, founded in 1929. For most of its history it was an amateur neighbourhood team, playing in the regional leagues under various names. Its rise began in the 1980s and 1990s, when the club, backed by the Paluani bakery company, climbed through the lower divisions and reached Serie B in 1994. Chievo shared the Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi with its city rival Hellas Verona.

In 2001 Chievo won promotion to Serie A for the first time, and its debut season became one of the great fairy tales of Italian football: the "Flying Donkeys" led the table in the autumn and finished fifth, qualifying for the UEFA Cup. The club established itself as a regular top-flight side for almost two decades, and in 2006 it reached the qualifying round of the UEFA Champions League after the Calciopoli scandal reshaped the final Serie A standings.

After relegation in 2019, the club ran into serious financial difficulties. In 2021 it was excluded from Serie B over unpaid tax debts and ceased its professional activity. A new club claiming its heritage later restarted from the amateur leagues, but the original AC ChievoVerona remains remembered as one of the most remarkable small-club success stories in Italian football.

name: Málaga CF
content:
Málaga CF is a Spanish football club from Málaga, Andalusia, playing its home matches at La Rosaleda Stadium. The club traces its roots to CD Málaga, founded in 1904, but the current entity was established on 25 May 1948 as Club Atlético Malagueño, originally the reserve team of CD Málaga. After CD Málaga was dissolved in 1992 because of its debts, Atlético Malagueño took over as the city's main club and in 1994 changed its name to Málaga Club de Fútbol.

The renamed club climbed quickly through the divisions and reached La Liga in 1999. In 2002 it won the UEFA Intertoto Cup and went on to reach the quarter-finals of the 2002–03 UEFA Cup. After a spell in the second tier, Málaga returned to the top flight in 2008, and in 2010 the club was bought by Qatari businessman Abdullah bin Nasser Al Thani, whose investment brought in well-known players and coach Manuel Pellegrini.

The club's greatest success came in the 2012–13 season, its debut in the UEFA Champions League: Málaga topped a group with Milan and Zenit, knocked out Porto in the round of 16 and were eliminated by Borussia Dortmund in the quarter-finals only by two stoppage-time goals. Financial problems and UEFA sanctions followed, the club was relegated in 2018, and it was later placed under judicial administration, continuing to compete in the Spanish professional leagues.
